  GENERAL FUND PURSUANT TO CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT
  CODE SECTION 50050-50057

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-116, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale to transfer unclaimed checks from their respective funds to the general fund
pursuant to California Government Code Section 50050-50057.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-116, a
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Palmdale to transfer unclaimed checks from
their respective funds to the general fund pursuant to California Government Code
Section 50050-50057.

BACKGROUND

Section 50050-50057 of the California Government Code states that “Except as
otherwise provided by law, money, excluding restitution to victims, that is not the
property of a local agency that remains unclaimed in its treasury or in the official custody
of its officers for three years is the property of the local agency after notice if not claimed
or if no verified complaint is filed and served. At any time after the expiration of the three-
year period, the treasurer of the local agency may cause a notice to be published once
a week for two successive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation published in the
local agency. At the expiration of the three-year period, money representing restitution
collected on behalf of victims shall be deposited into the Restitution Fund or used by the
local agency for purposes of victim services.” Government Code section 50053 allows
the City to transfer unclaimed funds in a special fund to the general fund.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-116
October 19, 2022
Page 2

DISCUSSION

The City Treasurer desires to follow the guidelines set by California Government Code
Section 50053 and the policy set forth by this department in relation to this section.
Section 50053 states “When any such money becomes the property of a local agency
and is in a special fund, the legislative body may transfer it to the general fund.” The
total combined number of unclaimed checks for the three-year period ending June 30,
2022, is $9,756.15.

FISCAL IMPACT
The total combined number of unclaimed checks for the three-year period ending June
30, 2022, is $9,756.15. This is the maximum amount that can be transferred to the
General Fund.

STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  B. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.
  C. Involve and expand engagement to enhance public oversight and
  transparency.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2022-114, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE APPROVING ENERGY
  FOR PALMDALE’S INDEPENDENT CHOICE INTEGRATED
  RESOURCE PLAN

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-114, a resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale approving Energy for Palmdale’s Independent Choice Integrated Resource
Plan.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-114 Energy for
Palmdale’s Independent Choice Integrated Resource Plan.

BACKGROUND

The City’s Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) Program, Energy for Palmdale’s
Independent Choice (EPIC), was established by the City Council through the adoption of
Resolution No. CC 2018-087 on December 4, 2018. EPIC began serving customers on
October 1, 2022.

DISCUSSION
Senate Bill (SB) 350, approved by the Governor on October 7, 2015, added, among other
actions, Public Code section 454.52 which established the requirement for load serving
entities, including CCAs, to file an Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) with the California
Public Utilities Commission (CPUC).

Additionally, SB 350 made revisions to the Renewables Portfolio Standards (RPS) for
California, with which EPIC will be required to comply. Specifically, SB 350 increased the
minimum renewable energy standards from 33% by December 31, 2020 to 50% by
December 31, 2030.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-114, a resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale approving Energy for Palmdale’s Independent Choice Integrated Resource
Plan
October 19, 2022
Page 2

To ensure CCAs are meeting these minimum standards, as well as meeting greenhouse
gas reduction targets as established by the California Air Resources Board, an IRP is
required to be filed with the CPUC for certification. The IRP looks out at a 10-year time
horizon and establishes a plan for EPIC’s procurement activities to meet the RPS and
greenhouse gas reduction targets. The IRP is strictly a forecasted plan and does not
commit EPIC to the specific actions identified to meet the RPS and greenhouse gas
reduction targets. As such, the CPUC requires the IRP to be revised every two years.
Palmdale approved its first IRP on September 1, 2020, and per SB 350 will be updated
and brought back to City Council for approval every two years.

California Choice Energy Authority and its technical consultants, on behalf of EPIC, have
been working closely with the CPUC to ensure the IRP as presented to City Council meets
all the requirements established by the CPUC. The proposed IRP, a completed copy of
which is on file in the Finance Department and will be posted to the EPIC website, follows
the required template as provided by the CPUC.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal I: Maintain effective public safety and protection for life, property and the
environment.
  C. Use a variety of methods to communicate timely, useful, and trusted information
  about city programs, services and policies.
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  A. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal health.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE THE ACQUISITION OF TAX DEFAULTED PROPERTY
  LOCATED ON THE SOUTHWEST CORNER OF AVENUE Q-3 AND
  6TH STREET EAST ALLEY (APN 3008-013-042 and 3008-013-043)
  THROUGH A CHAPTER 8 SALE AGREEMENT WITH LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY TREASURER AND TAX COLLECTOR.

ISSUE
Approve the acquisition of tax defaulted property located on the southwest corner of
Avenue Q-3 and 6th Street East Alley (APN 3008-013-042 and 3008-013-043) through
a Chapter 8 Agreement Sale with Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that City Council:

  1. Approve the acquisition of tax defaulted property (APN 3008-013-042 and
  3008-013-043) through a Chapter 8 Agreement Sale with Los Angeles County
  Treasurer and Tax Collector; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to prepare and execute all
  necessary documents to complete property acquisition.

BACKGROUND
Upon the failure of a property owner to meet the payment obligation of his or her property
tax, the LA County Treasurer and Tax Collector (TTC) sends the property owner a Notice
of Auction. The default opens a 5-year waiting period for residential property and 3-year
waiting period for non-residential commercial property during which the delinquent
taxes, interest, and penalties accumulate until redeemed. At the end of the 5 years for
residential property and 3 years for non-residential commercial property, if the tax is not
redeemed, the TTC has the power to sell the property. TTC conducts a tax defaulted
property auction twice per year in April and October.

As a public agency, the City of Palmdale can acquire property from the tax defaulted
property list if there is a public purpose for the property. To begin the process, a public
agency or nonprofit organization submits an Application to Purchase Tax-Defaulted
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: APN 3008-013-042 & 3008-013-043
October 19, 2022
Page 2

Property from the County to indicate which property the agency or organization is
interesting in purchasing. The City would also need to provide minutes from a public
meeting where the City Council approved the potential acquisition of the property. If the
City’s application is approved, the TTC will designate the City as “pre-qualified” and
forward an Agreement Sale packet, along with instructions on how to complete the forms
and a checklist of requirements. The process can take anywhere between six and nine
months to complete and there is no guarantee that the property will be sold to the City.

DISCUSSION
The City reviewed the tax defaulted property list and identified two parcels that the
City would be interested in purchasing. The parcels are located on the southwest
corner of Avenue Q-3 and 6th Street East Alley (APN’s 3008-013-042 and 3008-013-
043). These parcels are located within the Palmdale Transit Area Specific Plan
(PTASP) and will support the future development of the California High Speed Rail
Palmdale Station. The acquisition of the properties will also allow the City to complete
future street widening and pedestrian improvements along sections of Avenue Q-3
and 6th Street East Alley.

The property purchase will only be completed if the application is fully approved by
TTC, and the property owners do not reclaim the property before the Chapter 8
Agreement Sale is closed. The property owner has the duration of the process to
rectify their defaulted property tax status on the properties. The final purchase price
shall include all costs of the sale, and the amount of outstanding taxes and penalties
accrued up until the Agreement Sale is finalized.

FISCAL IMPACT
Not to exceed $75,000. The total cost includes the amount of outstanding taxes and
penalties, auction fees and other minimal costs needed to complete the property
acquisition. Funds are available in account 15761101-737133

BACKGROUND
Project No. 813 refurbishes the building at 38448 Sierra Highway, Palmdale, CA 93550,
to house the Palmdale Film Stages. The improvements include, but are not limited to,
building interior and exterior renovations, electrical upgrades, and associated parking and
accessibility improvements.

DISCUSSION
This project has one previous Supplemental Agreement that was approved
administratively under the authority of City Manager for $30,343.45. Supplemental
Agreement No. 1 included the addition of a bid item for concrete foundation work that was

determined to be required due to field verification after bid award, and an increase in bid
quantity for bollards due to an error in the bid schedule.

Supplemental Agreement No. 2 includes three (3) changes to the project scope as
outlined below.

The first change relates to the addition of an interior green screen for filming use. The
green screen was not included within the original scope, plans or specs, but was highly
recommended by the City’s Film liaison to attract more use to the facility. The cost for
this change includes the materials and labor to construct the green screen.

The second change relates to the repainting the exterior of the building. The originally
approved colors for the building exterior were deemed unacceptable and will be replaced
with a more muted color palette. Additionally, the north wall will be added to the paint
scope, as it was not originally included in this cost item. The cost for this change includes
the materials and labor to repaint the exterior of the building.

The third change relates to the replacement of the exterior doors. The originally approved
exterior doors included glass panels, but with growing security concerns, the exterior
doors be replaced with solid door panels. The cost for this change includes the material
and labor to replace the exterior doors.
